claim: VeRPO treats per-unit-test partial success (passing a subset of hidden tests) as a first-class, exploitable signal for RL reward shaping in code generation, confirming that partial-pass granularity is a recognized, actively-researched axis distinct from binary pass/fail -- but for reward optimization, not for confidence calibration.
stance_target: whether per-requirement/per-test partial correctness is a novel axis DPRC discovered, or an already-recognized dimension in code-LLM research
scope_conditions: RL post-training for code generation, hidden unit-test suites
quoted_support: by dynamically estimating the difficulty weight of each unit test based on the execution statistics during training, a dense reward is derived from the sum of weights of the passed unit tests

claim: VeRPO's 'calibration' terminology refers to correcting a cardinality bias in the reward function (easy-test overcounting), not to model-expressed confidence calibration (ECE/AUROC/Brier) -- the paper never trains or evaluates a confidence output.
stance_target: VeRPO as a directly competing confidence-calibration baseline for DPRC
scope_conditions: VeRPO scope, RL reward shaping only
quoted_support: The framework addresses an inherent cardinality bias in partial-success rewards: redundant easy tests dominate the optimization baseline by sheer count
